chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who accuses another man of adultery, so he pardons him and makes him free from that. Then it occurs to him that he should bring him forward until he is whipped. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no Hadd (penalty) for him after the pardon.'

So I said to him: 'What is your view if he said, 'O son of the adulteress', so he pardoned him and left that to Allah?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If his mother was alive, it is not for him to pardon; the pardon is for his mother. Whenever she wishes, she takes her right.'
He (peace be upon him) said: 'If his mother had died, then he is the guardian of her affairs, and his pardon is valid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on pardoning an accusation of adultery (Qadhf) when the accuser says 'son of the adulteress'?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the specific mechanics of 'Afw' (pardon) in the Hadd penalty for Qadhf, distinguishing between the accuser's personal right and the rights of the mother. It establishes that if the mother is alive, the accuser cannot unilaterally pardon until she consents, as she holds the primary right; however, upon her death, the father (or guardian) inherits this right, validating his pardon. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the preservation of individual dignity and the transfer of legal rights upon death.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Sama’at who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who slandered the man with the adultery. So he excused him from it and he made him to be free from that. Is it for him to begin (proceedings) that he can bring him up until he is whipped (for it)?’ So heasws said: ‘There is no Penalty (Hadd) for him after the excusing’.

So I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘What is your view that he said, ‘O son of the adulteress’, so he excused from it and left that to Allah<sup>azwj</sup>’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If his mother was alive, so it is not for him that he should excuse. The excusing it is for his mother whenever she so desires to take her right’.
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘If his mother had died, so he would be the guardian of her affairs, his excusing would be allowed’.
